captions.text: In Map Visualizations, start on Library and search for Calls by type.
Read the matching template description: it shows recent calls
as dots coloured by call type.
Select that result, then open Customize.
The heading changes from the earlier Call hot zones view to Calls by type.
Choosing a template gives you a starting configuration that you can
inspect before saving your own view.

scenes.title: Review the date and time scope

captions.text: Under When, this template has Date range set to Last ninety days.
Days of the week and Hours of the day are shown below it.
The page explains that leaving those buttons unselected includes every day
required_labels: Leave everything unselected to include every day and hour. Times are in your department's time zone.

captions.text: and hour, using the department time zone.
Keep this time scope for the exercise.
Check these controls whenever you compare demand, because a different time
window answers a different question.

scenes.title: Choose the call type and observe the changed result

captions.text: Scroll within Customize to Which calls and open Call types.
The unfiltered view shows seventeen calls and eighty-two percent with a location.
Check Investigation, then close the selector.
Its button now reads Investigation, and the result changes to eight calls with
sixty-three percent having a location.
This shows the effect of the selected filter on the same time window.
The other visible selectors remain All in this exercise.

scenes.title: Distinguish matching activity from mapped activity

captions.text: Compare the filtered summary with the map legend.
Eight calls match the filter, while the Investigation legend
contains five located entries.
The summary rounds that location completeness to sixty-three percent.
A map shows where located activity appears; its dots do not account for
calls that lack a usable location.
Check this measure before treating a sparse map as evidence
that little work occurred.
These numbers describe the fictional recorded dataset.

scenes.title: Inspect the actual layer display choices

captions.text: In Layers, review the enabled Calls layer.
Data is Calls, described as one point per call at the call location.
required_labels: One point per call, at the call's location.

captions.text: Show as is Dots, Color by is Call type, and Value is Count.
Opacity and Dot size are separate display controls below these choices.
Keep the shown configuration here.
Reading the data source and display choices together helps you explain
what the symbols represent, rather than judging only their appearance.

scenes.title: Name the private view and save it

captions.text: Select Save as new.
In Save as a new visualization, enter the fictional name shown here
and a Description that records the purpose, date scope and filter.
Leave Share with the whole department unchecked for this private exercise.
The choice is visible beside the form, so check it deliberately before saving.
This walkthrough saves a view for the current user.
Select Save.
Open Library and check Saved visualizations.
Under My visualizations, the named Investigation demand review
appears with its description and Only visible to you label.
The same saved name is now the page heading.
These are returned application results after the save,
rather than the unsaved form.
Confirm the intended entry and visibility label before using the view again.

scenes.title: Reopen and verify the retained settings

captions.text: Open the saved visualization in a fresh page and return to Customize.
Date range still reads Last ninety days.
Scroll to Call types and check that Investigation is retained.
Then inspect the layer again: Calls, Dots, Call type and Count remain selected.
This reopening check verifies the stored configuration beyond
the form where it was prepared.
It does not depend on remembering the settings from the earlier screen.

scenes.title: Read the saved map and its supporting summary

captions.text: With the side panel closed, read the saved map and Investigation legend together.
Scroll below it to see the eight-call total, location percentage,
When calls come in grid, and Most common call types summary.
The latter still shows Investigation and eight.
Response-time cards contain dashes in this view, and the page explains
their data and layer requirements.
A dash is not a measured zero-minute response.
Use the displayed results for the question this view actually answers.

scenes.title: Use repeatable views across department types

captions.text: The same process can support community paramedicine and mental health response
planning, search-and-rescue activity reviews, security service demand, wildland
contractor workload, industrial emergency response, and fire and E M S departments.
Choose the permitted call types and time scope relevant to your team.
Inspect the display settings, check location completeness, save the intended
visibility, and reopen the result.
A useful planning view is one whose filters and data
limitations you can explain.
